verse.text: Then he said to them, “Watch out! Be on your guard against all kinds of greed; life does not consist in an abundance of possessions.”

reflection.scripture: Then he said to them, “Watch out! Be on your guard against all kinds of greed; life does not consist in an abundance of possessions.”
reflection.observation: Jesus interrupts a family dispute about inheritance with a sharp warning — not about money itself, but about the heart posture behind it. The phrase 'all kinds of greed' is broad: it covers the obvious (hoarding wealth) and the subtle (quiet comparison, envy, the endless chase for 'just a little more'). Jesus doesn't say possessions are evil — He says they don't define life. That's a different metric entirely.
reflection.application: Today, notice what you're measuring life by. Is it follower counts, upgrades, savings, status? Or peace, presence, relationships, faithfulness? Set one boundary: before the day ends, identify one area where 'more' has quietly become your scoreboard — and choose gratitude instead.
reflection.prayer: Lord, guard my heart from the greed that whispers I'm not enough yet. Teach me to measure my life by what lasts — love, faith, presence with You. Help me hold possessions loosely and people tightly. Amen.
